questions.q: Which type of sewing machine is operated by the continuous movement of the user's feet on a pedal?
questions.explain: A treadle sewing machine is mechanically powered by a foot pedal (treadle) which the user pumps up and down to drive the needle mechanism.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles

questions.q: Which part of the sewing machine is responsible for holding the fabric flat and firmly in place while sewing?
questions.explain: The presser foot holds the fabric down firmly against the feed dog (the metal teeth), ensuring the fabric moves smoothly and evenly while the needle stitches.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles

questions.q: What is the function of the 'balance wheel' on a manual sewing machine?
options: It holds the thread spool at the top of the machine.
It turns to control the movement of the needle up and down.
It automatically cuts the thread when finished.
It winds the bobbin inside the bobbin case.
questions.explain: The balance wheel (or handwheel) is located on the right side of the machine and is rotated to manually raise and lower the needle and control the machine's initial movement.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles

questions.q: The small metal spool that holds the lower thread underneath the needle plate of a sewing machine is called the:
questions.explain: The bobbin is a tiny spool placed in the lower part of the sewing machine. It provides the lower thread, which locks with the upper thread to form a stitch.
questions.exam: BECE Pre-Vocational Studies: Family Living, Child Care & Textiles

questions.q: When choosing a sewing machine to buy for home use, which of the following factors is most important to consider?
options: The color of the machine casing.
The user's purpose, skill level, and available budget.
The amount of noise the machine makes when breaking.
Buying the most expensive industrial model available.
questions.explain: The primary factors in selecting a sewing machine are what you intend to use it for (e.g., mending vs. professional tailoring), the skill level of the user, and the cost.

questions.q: To keep a sewing machine running smoothly and prevent its metal parts from rusting, it should be regularly:
options: Washed with soapy water and a sponge.
Oiled with appropriate machine oil and dusted.
questions.explain: Regular oiling lubricates the moving metal parts, reducing friction, preventing rust, and ensuring the machine operates smoothly.

questions.q: What is the primary reason for covering a sewing machine when it is not in use?
options: To prevent it from catching fire.
To protect it from dust, lint, and moisture.
To stop the oil from drying up.
questions.explain: Dust and lint can enter the machine's moving parts and cause damage over time. A cover protects the machine and keeps it clean.

questions.q: In garment construction, what is a 'seam'?
options: A line of stitching that joins two or more pieces of fabric together.
A hole cut in the fabric for the head to pass through.
The frayed edge of a woven fabric.
A decorative patch ironed onto the dress.
questions.explain: A seam is the basic structural element in sewing where two pieces of fabric are stitched together, such as the side seam of a shirt or dress.

questions.q: Which term describes the process of folding the raw edge of a garment (like a skirt) and sewing it down to prevent fraying?
questions.explain: Hemming involves turning under the raw edge of a piece of fabric and stitching it flat. It gives a neat finish to the bottom of skirts, trousers, and sleeves.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a 'dart' in garment construction?
options: To add a permanent color stripe to the fabric.
To shape flat fabric to fit the natural curves of the body, such as the bust or waist.
To securely attach buttons to a shirt.
To cut complex curves using scissors.
questions.explain: A dart is a folded and stitched wedge of fabric used to control shape and fullness, allowing flat two-dimensional fabric to fit three-dimensionally around body curves.

questions.q: When making a simple baby dress, which of the following is commonly used as a fastening to make dressing the baby easier?
options: Press studs (snap fasteners) or small flat buttons
questions.explain: Fastenings secure garment openings. Press studs (snaps) and flat buttons are safe and practical fastenings used in baby clothes to easily put on and take off garments.

questions.q: Which machine part controls the tightness or looseness of the upper thread as it forms a stitch?
questions.explain: The tension disc or regulator adjusts how tightly the machine holds the upper thread. Proper tension is required so stitches don't pucker or loop loosely.
